confirmed.title: `fix` with an empty re-transcription wipes the fragment and marks the feedback resolved
confirmed.evidence: cli.py:202-216 has no check that the new note list is non-empty. Stub run (scratchpad/lens2/fix_empty.py; refute-l2-a/t.py) → 'before (1): D4 / after (0): (none) / updated ... / feedback F1 resolved', rc 0; calls PATCH in-progress, PUT notes=[], PATCH resolved. Server accepts it: apps/server/src/app.ts:248 body `z.array(LessonNote)` without min; repo.ts:165-178 deletes the fragment's notes. If that fragment held all notes, validateLessonInput fails notes.min(1) (packages/core/src/lesson.ts:77) → plain Error → 500 (app.ts:109-113).
confirmed.failure_scenario: An agent runs `transcribe fix` with a high --onset-threshold, a wrong offsetSec or on a quiet passage; the engine returns nothing. The fragment's notes are deleted, the user's 'sounds wrong' report is closed as resolved, and the fragment shows no keys.
confirmed.fix_hint: Refuse to PUT when the new list is empty; warn / require --force when it shrinks below ~50% of the old one; never resolve the feedback in that case.
confirmed.refuters: both confirmed; severity major (refuter A) / minor (refuter B) → kept major: silent data loss + auto-resolved report

confirmed.title: `fix` clamps boundary notes to end-0.001, which origin/main's TIME_EPS=0.002 assigns to the NEXT fragment
confirmed.evidence: lesson.py:83 `t = min(max(n.start, start), end - 0.001)`. origin/main packages/core/src/steps.ts:35 TIME_EPS = 0.002, :39 notesInRange `n.start < end - TIME_EPS`; apps/web/src/audio/player.ts:217,:251 use TIME_EPS. origin/main apps/server/src/repo.ts:174 still deletes with 1e-6. Repro against main's core (refute-l3-b/r1.mts): notes {0:60, 5.399:72, 5.4:63}, fragments [0,5.4),[5.4,10] → frag0 [60], frag1 [72, 63]. Branch merge-base 8a070bf predates main's 8261619 (the TIME_EPS change), so this appears only after merge.
confirmed.failure_scenario: After merging main, `fix k` inserts a boundary note at end-0.001; the app plays it in fragment k+1, so the fix for k seems to drop it and k+1 gains an extra key. `fix k+1` cannot remove it (server's 1e-6 delete window counts it as k's); only a re-fix of k does.
confirmed.fix_hint: Rebase on main; clamp to at most end - 2*TIME_EPS (or drop new notes at/after end instead of clamping); use one shared EPS=0.002 in notes.py in_window and lesson.py's outside filter. Main-side follow-up: repo.replaceFragmentNotes should use TIME_EPS instead of 1e-6.
confirmed.refuters: both confirmed; severity major (refuter B) / minor (refuter A: narrow trigger, recoverable by re-fixing k) → kept major as a post-merge integration bug

confirmed.title: yt-dlp has no size or duration limit and always downloads the whole video
confirmed.evidence: audio.py:55-75 argv: --no-playlist ... -f bestaudio/best -x --audio-format wav ...; no --max-filesize, no `--match-filter duration<…`, no --download-sections. --start/--end only crop afterwards (cli.py:92-95). Whole-file caching per video id is deliberate (README.md:9; reused by fix).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A multi-hour livestream is downloaded and converted in full (~318 MB/hour of mono 44.1 kHz WAV, inferred) even with `--start 0 --end 30`; without --end the whole file goes to the CPU model.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add `--match-filter 'duration < 1200'` (or a --max-duration flag) and --max-filesize; refuse longer inputs without an explicit flag.
confirmed.refuters: both confirmed; both suggest minor (lens said major) → minor

confirmed.title: Non-API errors end in a Python traceback with exit 1, the same code as 'no notes found'
confirmed.evidence: cli.py:324-330 main() catches only ApiError. Stub runs: `youtube https://example.com/x` → ValueError; `audio /nonexistent.wav` → FileNotFoundError; RuntimeError (_need, _source_audio cli.py:181) and CalledProcessError (audio.py:75,97,115 check=True) also escape. cli.py:99 returns 1 for 'no notes found'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An agent driving the CLI gets a stack trace and an ambiguous exit 1 for ordinary errors (bad URL, missing file, yt-dlp 403).
confirmed.fix_hint: Catch ValueError, FileNotFoundError, RuntimeError, CalledProcessError, OSError in main(); print one line; use a distinct exit code.

confirmed.title: `fix --feedback` leaves the item stuck in 'in-progress' when anything fails before the PUT
confirmed.evidence: cli.py:186-187 PATCHes in-progress before get_lesson, the fragment range check (return 2 at :192), _source_audio (:195) and the PUT; no try/finally. `transcribe feedback` lists only 'open' by default (cli.py:304). Stub: `fix x 5 --feedback F1` → rc 2, only call PATCH in-progress (refute-l2-a/t.py).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A wrong fragment index, a lesson without a replayable source, or a yt-dlp/API failure drops the item out of the default open queue; it is silently forgotten.
confirmed.fix_hint: Mark in-progress only right before the PUT, or reset to 'open' in a finally block on failure.
confirmed.lens: correctness+security (also raised by claims and integration lenses)

confirmed.title: `fix` cannot work on a lesson made by `audio`/`midi` without --source-url, and the docs don't say so
confirmed.evidence: cli.py:148 load_local(a.file, a.source_url) and audio.py:99 store url only from --source-url; lesson.py:55-56 sets url only if truthy. cli.py:175-181 _source_audio raises RuntimeError when there is no YouTube id or existing local path. README.md:61-65 and SKILL.md §3 describe fix without that precondition. Read, not run (would need a recording).
confirmed.failure_scenario: User transcribes a local m4a, reports a fragment; the agent runs `fix … --feedback <id>` → traceback and a feedback item stuck in-progress.
confirmed.fix_hint: Store the local path (or a file:// URL) as source.url when --source-url is absent, or refuse `fix` up front with a clear message; document the precondition.

confirmed.title: MIDI import keeps pitches outside 21–108, so one stray note makes the API reject the whole import
confirmed.evidence: midi_io.py:26-37 keeps every non-drum note; cmd_midi (cli.py:152-172) never calls drop_out_of_range (cleanup.py:38). zod pitch int 21..108 (packages/core/src/lesson.ts:18). Repro: MIDI with pitches 15,60,120 → read_midi keeps all (refute-l2-b/t.py); `midi x.mid --dry-run --save-json` saved pitch 10 (refute-l2-a/t.py). The server's own MIDI importer skips <21/>108 (packages/core/src/midi.ts:36), so the tool is inconsistent with the app.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A General-MIDI arrangement with one note below A0 or above C8 → 400 'notes.N.pitch' → exit 3; nothing is imported.
confirmed.fix_hint: Apply drop_out_of_range (or octave-fold) in cmd_midi and print how many notes were dropped.

confirmed.title: `fix` pulls a next-fragment note into this fragment when the re-transcription hears it at a different pitch
confirmed.evidence: lesson.py:76-84 keeps new notes with onset in [end, end+tol) and clamps them to end-0.001 unless an outside old note has the SAME pitch within tol (:81). Repro: fragment_replacement(new=[60@1.01, 62@1.49, 65@2.03], old=[60@1.0, 62@1.5, 64@2.0], 1.0, 2.0) → [(60,1.01),(62,1.49),(65,1.999)] (both refuters' scripts).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The re-transcription mis-hears the first note of the next fragment (octave/overtone error); that wrong note is inserted at the end of the fixed fragment while the next fragment keeps its own, so the user plays an extra note. Combined with the TIME_EPS finding above, after merge it even shows up in the next fragment.
confirmed.fix_hint: Skip new notes within tol of a bound when any outside old note (any pitch) sits within tol on the far side, or do not accept notes past `end` at all.

confirmed.title: `show` and fix's before/after use a 1e-6 window, while origin/main plays fragments with TIME_EPS=0.002
confirmed.evidence: notes.py:54-56 `start - 1e-6 <= n.start < end - 1e-6`, docstring 'the fragment rule of the lesson format'; callers cli.py:205 (fix before) and cli.py:249 (show). It matched the merge-base core (8a070bf steps.ts:33) and still matches the server delete window (repo.ts:174), but origin/main steps.ts:39 and player.ts:251 use TIME_EPS.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A note with onset 0–2 ms below a bound is listed by `show N` under N but played by the app in N+1, which can mislead which fragment to fix. No data loss.
confirmed.fix_hint: Use one EPS constant equal to core TIME_EPS (0.002) in in_window and fragment_replacement after rebasing.
